clue.text: Old English pot's possibly an old bucket

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters, so they are reshuffled

blocks.note: OE is the standard abbreviation for Old English
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon pot might once have served as a pail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an old' leads into the definition: stoope is an archaic spelling of stoup, a drinking vessel or bucket.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoup was a pail or flagon for liquids; stoope is an archaic variant spelling of that vessel.

clue.text: Means of bringing water to the fire? River is trapped in towel, maybe

definitions.text: Means of bringing water to the fire?

indicators.note: trapped in describes something held inside another, so river and is go within the drying word

blocks.note: a towel is one example of something that dries, a dryer
R is the abbreviation for river
taken as written

explanation.surface: Firefighting equipment, with a river caught up in a bath towel.
explanation.walkthrough: A dry riser is a vertical empty pipe in a tall building that firefighters connect hoses to, carrying water up to upper floors.
explanation.definitionFit: Firefighters pump water into a dry riser at ground level so it can be delivered to hoses on the floor where the blaze is.

clue.text: Father of Paris who's mostly worried over head of Minotaur

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the name is kept
worried here means shaken about, so the shortened name is jumbled
in a down clue, over places the first part above the letter that follows
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the Trojan prince's name, taken as written; 'who' refers back to it
the first letter of the Cretan bull-man's name

explanation.surface: The Trojan prince's father is anxious about a Cretan monster.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris does double duty: the definition names Priam as his father, and 'who' points back to the same word as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Priam, king of Troy, was the father of Paris, whose abduction of Helen caused the Trojan War.

clue.text: See 12 across
They're seen in Verona and Ercolano, for starters, with springs

definitions.text: They're seen in Verona and Ercolano, for starters, with springs

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so the first letters of the two Italian places are taken

blocks.note: first letter of the northern Italian city
first letter of the town near Naples
spas are places with mineral springs

explanation.surface: Things you spot around two Italian towns, and they have springs fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: Ercolano is the modern town on the site of Herculaneum. The whole clue also describes the scooters, which have sprung suspension.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespas are the classic Italian motor scooters, a common sight in Italian towns and built with suspension springs.

clue.text: Beef circumambulatin' the mountain reared!

indicators.note: reared means raised up, so in a down clue the mountain word is read upwards

blocks.note: the song line 'comin' round the mountain' supplies the word that goes round, and says it goes round
an alp is a mountain

explanation.surface: A singer rearing up, mid-song about coming round the mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: It echoes 'She'll Be Comin' Round the Mountain': circumambulating means going round, so the dropped-g word is COMIN around the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is slang for grumbling or protesting, which is the same as complaining.

clue.text: Porridge cooking technique?

blocks.note: British slang for a prison sentence, and also the oat breakfast that has to be stirred while it cooks
read straight, a method of preparing food; it also tells you the second half is a way of cooking

explanation.surface: A question about the right way to make porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for time in prison, and so is STIR; add FRY, a cooking method, and you get the quick-fry wok technique.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir-fry is a method of cooking food quickly in a wok over high heat, so it is a culinary technique.

clue.text: "Def" worked with more boldness

indicators.note: worked suggests material kneaded or reshaped, so the letters of Def and more are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hip-hop slang being used with extra swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom can mean frankness or lack of restraint in speech or manner, which is a kind of boldness.

clue.text: The same ram job demolished vertical member

indicators.note: something demolished is broken up, so the letters of ram job are scrambled

blocks.note: DO is short for ditto, meaning the same as above
taken as written, the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A battering-ram assault knocks down an upright, just as before.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorjamb is the upright side post of a door frame, a vertical structural piece.

clue.text: They're worn in New York — sox, bra, then, out East

indicators.note: out means the east letter is dropped from the garments' letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.walkthrough: The Bronx is one of New York's boroughs; 'worn' doubles as the signal that the garment letters are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Hats from one of New York City's boroughs are headgear worn in the city.

clue.text: What give "spout" (mobile — that's a little phone)?

definitions.text: What give "spout" (mobile — that's a little phone)?

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so the letters of spout are shifted around
only a little of the word phone is used: its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
its opening letter is all that is taken

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what makes a phone talk, with a playful aside about mobiles.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes what lets a little mobile phone talk again: credit added to it. Top-ups are the prepaid credit added to a pay-as-you-go mobile.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay-as-you-go phones need credit added before calls can be made, and those additions of credit are what let the handset speak.

clue.text: Literary "ante" in story: O, wot, about a little David?

definitions.note: ante is a playful spelling of aunt, so this asks for an aunt from a book

indicators.note: about here means around in disorder, so all the gathered letters are rearranged
only a little of the name David is used: its first letter

blocks.note: a poker ante is a stake, a BET
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
its opening letter is all that is taken

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader asks what's going on in a tale about a small boy named David.
explanation.walkthrough: The word ante does two jobs: with Literary it reads as a jokey spelling of aunt, and as a poker stake it gives BET. Betsey Trotwood is David Copperfield's great-aunt in Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Betsy Trotwood is the formidable great-aunt who takes in the young hero of Dickens's David Copperfield, so she is a fictional relative.

clue.text: One of those Paul addressed in passage with noted alternative by name

blocks.note: a col is a pass between mountains
ossia is the musical term (noted, as in set in notes) for an alternative passage a performer may play
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: St Paul writing to a congregation, giving another option for a reading by name.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossia, Italian for 'or else', marks an alternative version in a musical score. Paul's Epistle to the Colossians is a New Testament letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colossians, people of Colossae, received one of the New Testament letters attributed to the apostle Paul.

clue.text: Wanting it too much

blocks.note: it is a coy word for sex, so this is desiring sex
excess, more than is wanted or proper

explanation.walkthrough: The innocent-looking 'it' is the old euphemism for sex, as in the phrase 'the It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone oversexed has an excessive sex drive, so they want sex more than is usual or proper.

clue.text: Museum with 'er indoors? A bit of help — it keeps NZ shoppers dry

indicators.note: indoors puts 'er inside the museum's name
only a bit of help is used: its first letter

blocks.note: the V and A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum
'er is a dropped-h her, the comic 'er indoors meaning a wife
its opening letter is all that is taken

explanation.surface: A wife at a museum, a little assistance, and a shop canopy in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Er indoors is British slang for one's wife. Shop fronts in New Zealand towns commonly have verandahs over the pavement to shelter shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: In New Zealand a verandah is the roof projecting over a shop's pavement, sheltering shoppers from the rain.

clue.text: See 14

explanation.surface: A famous soprano once sat for a portrait as a fiddler.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarah Brightman is a British singer known for musical theatre. Sate is an old form of sat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo de Sarasate was a celebrated nineteenth-century Spanish violin virtuoso and composer.

clue.text: Zola heroine, a right twit

blocks.note: first meaning: the courtesan title character of Émile Zola's novel ...
second meaning: British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A reader's harsh verdict on a famous French literary heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Zola's 1880 novel is named after its heroine, and in British slang a nana is a silly person or idiot.

clue.text: Newbie's earmarked for virtual punch-up, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells you the answer is spelt as something else is said

blocks.note: a fight by Neo, hero of the virtual-reality film The Matrix

explanation.surface: A newcomer is singled out for an online scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: Neo is the hero of The Matrix, who fights inside a computer simulation, so a virtual punch-up is a Neo fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a beginner or novice, the same as a newbie in online slang.

clue.text: South African of the old guard

blocks.note: first meaning: a native of Pretoria, South Africa's administrative capital
second meaning: a variant spelling of praetorian, belonging to the Roman emperor's bodyguard

explanation.surface: Describing an old-school conservative from South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old guard' suggests a die-hard traditionalist, but here it is the Praetorian Guard of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pretorian is someone from Pretoria, and the same spelling is an accepted variant of praetorian, the emperor's elite guard.

clue.text: Scotch or Lancastrian's particular bodily excrescence?

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, to put an end to or foil
second meaning: in Lancashire dialect 'the' shortens to t', so a specific wart is t'wart, said like the answer

explanation.surface: Whisky, or a Lancashire person's own particular growth on the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch looks like whisky but is the verb meaning to stamp out. Northern English speech clips 'the' to t', so 'the wart' is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to frustrate or stop it, which is what thwarting it means.

clue.text: Another place where tests are conducted

blocks.note: first meaning: MPs' traditional way of referring to the House of ... from the Commons
second meaning: ..., the London cricket ground that hosts Test matches

explanation.surface: Suggesting a different venue for running examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Commons, members avoid naming the upper house and call it 'another place'. Lord's is London's famous cricket ground, and Tests are international cricket matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses rest on the same word: the parliamentary chamber of peers and the cricket ground named after Thomas Lord.

clue.text: Ducks are somehow about to pass away? On the contrary

definitions.note: used as a single term of address, so it matches a singular answer

indicators.note: somehow means in some other way, so the letters of are are rearranged
about would put the jumbled word round the dying word
reverses the stated arrangement: the dying word goes round the jumbled one

blocks.note: to die
taken as written, the three letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some ducks are about to die, then doubting it.
explanation.walkthrough: Ducks is a British term of endearment, as in 'thanks, ducks'. 'On the contrary' flips the order of 'are about to pass away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks and dearie are both affectionate British forms of address, the kind used by a friendly shopkeeper.

clue.text: Setter could be wasting time using no superfluous words

explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies a wordy setter, while the answer means the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse writing is brief and concise, without unnecessary words.

clue.text: Kelvin's at this moment bipolar — neither 'x' nor 'y'

definitions.note: a plural noun phrase: values that are not the algebra variables

blocks.note: K is the symbol for the kelvin, the unit of temperature
now means at the present moment
having both poles, north and south, abbreviated N and S

explanation.surface: A man named Kelvin is currently manic-depressive, and somehow not a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra, x and y are the classic unknowns, so quantities that are neither are the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: In an equation the given values are knowns, in contrast to the unknown variables conventionally written x and y.

explanation.definitionFit: Szechwan, now usually written Sichuan, is a large province in south-west China.

clue.text: South African shootists about? (Ho, no!)
